name: writeFile
description: Write a file; payload carries the bytes (overwrites any existing content). Bytes may arrive inline as `content` (array<integer>) or via a transferred message port. With `atomic`, the bytes land in a temp file that then replaces the target, so a crash mid-write never leaves a torn file. With `ifMatch` the write is a compare-and-swap: it goes ahead only while the file still exists with exactly ifMatch.size bytes and an mtime within 1 ms of ifMatch.mtimeMs, and otherwise fails with the distinct code PRECONDITION_FAILED (nothing written); a successful ifMatch write answers { ok: true, mtimeMs, size } — the stat to pass as the next ifMatch. `ifMatch` is listed in the host manifest's `primitives` as fs.writeFile.ifMatch: an older host would IGNORE the field and write unconditionally, so the guest must not send it unless that entry is present.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: Bytes to write. May arrive inline as an array of integers in the payload, OR via a transferred MessagePort that delivers an ArrayBuffer.

inputs.name: atomic
inputs.description: Write via a temp file + replace (base::ImportantFileWriter) instead of in place, so a crash mid-write never leaves a partially written target. Additive, ignore-if-absent: an older host writes in place as before. Used for the session `meta.json`.

inputs.name: ifMatch
inputs.description: { mtimeMs, size } — the stat the caller last read. See the action description.
